channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: O relator da ação do PT contra Flávio Bolsonaro no TSE
item.description: The president of the TSE, Kassio Nunes Marques, has been appointed as rapporteur of a representation filed by the PT, PCdoB, and PV against Flávio Bolsonaro and other PL allies over alleged coordinated disinformation about electronic voting machines. The action claims they decontextualized a U.S. document on Venezuela to falsely link Smartmatic to Brazilian elections, despite the TSE repeatedly denying any connection between the company and Brazil’s voting system. The parties are seeking removal of content, platform measures, and a fine of BRL 30,000 per target.

item.title: Como ausência de Lula pode afetar participação de Flávio em debates
item.description: The potential absence of President Lula in the first-round televised debates could hinder Flávio Bolsonaro's participation, as he intends to debate only if Lula is present. Flávio's campaign views a direct confrontation with Lula as the main justification for his presence, while Lula's team evaluates participation on a case-by-case basis, with the Band debate on August 16 as a possible test. The strategy is also shaped by the likelihood that other center-right candidates could leave Lula isolated in the debates.

item.title: Urnas em questão
item.description: A Metrópoles poll of 982 readers shows 87.4% trust in the honesty and security of Brazil’s electronic voting system, while 12.6% express distrust. The article briefly mentions Flávio Bolsonaro as a candidate seeking a running mate and Lula, without elaborating on their positions. The overall tone is neutral, focusing on public perception of electoral integrity.

item.title: Entorno de Lula já trabalha com possibilidade de votação da PEC 6x1 ficar para depois da eleição
item.description: Lula’s inner circle is considering delaying the vote on the PEC 6x1 and other government priorities until after the October elections, due to a disengaged Congress and strained relations with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre. Some allies see this as a campaign opportunity to blame Congress for inaction, while others urge pushing for votes before the election to prevent amendments. The Planalto is monitoring the situation and weighing strategies to leverage public mobilization around the PEC 6x1.

item.title: Veto a encontro entre Flávio e Bolsonaro divide eleitores
item.description: A PoderData survey conducted between July 18 and 20, 2026 reveals that Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes’ decision to prohibit contact between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and former President Jair Bolsonaro until after the first round of elections has divided public opinion: among the 55% aware of the measure, 45% deemed it 'correct' and 42% 'incorrect', with 13% offering no opinion. The ban followed Flávio’s publication of a supportive letter from his father on social media, which Moraes ruled a violation of a prior restraining order against Bolsonaro’s use of third parties to post online.

item.title: O PT e os debates presidenciais na TV
item.description: The PT has not yet finalized Lula's participation in the 2026 presidential debates, but indicates it will follow the 2022 model of up to five debates. The decision will depend on Lula's polling performance: if he is doing well, he may opt out; if poorly, he will likely attend all. The article is subscriber-only.

item.title: Lula quer aval da equipe econômica em plano de governo para acalmar mercado
item.description: President Lula seeks to avoid market unrest by submitting his re-election government plan to review by the current economic team, including Dario Durigan, Bruno Moretti, and Esther Dweck, as well as former minister Fernando Haddad. This follows comments by Sérgio Gabrielli, the plan’s coordinator and former Petrobras president, which caused discomfort among financial market agents. The goal is to ensure the final document is perceived as economically responsible and stable.

item.title: O telefonema de Flávio Bolsonaro a Garotinho sobre a ‘noite das astronautas’ de Vorcaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro called Anthony Garotinho from Buenos Aires to deny his involvement in the alleged 'astronauts' night' and asked him to formally state he did not appear in the video. Garotinho reaffirmed on July 2 that, in the 12-minute segment he accessed, there were no images of Flávio Bolsonaro, and that he never claimed otherwise. The video, previously shared by Michelle Bolsonaro, shows Garotinho commenting on an unverified material about a party organized by Daniel Vorcaro, with claims of political participation and foreign women wearing space helmets.

item.title: Mariza Leão: 'Barretão está entre nós e dentro de nós'
item.description: The article highlights the legacy of Luiz Carlos Barreto, a leader of Brazilian cinema, who fought for a strong industrial policy for the audiovisual sector, defending national cultural sovereignty. Despite his efforts in engaging with authorities and promoting initiatives like the National Cinema Institute and the Audiovisual Law, he expressed disappointment at the end of his life due to the lack of commitment from public officials and the absence of a true industrial policy for the sector, even with Lula's promises of a 'potent cultural industry'.

item.title: Charge do Aroeira
item.description: The Aroeira cartoon, published in Noblat's Blog, highlights that Flávio Bolsonaro's heart beats faster, suggesting anxiety or enthusiasm, while Lula's beats slower, indicating calm or disinterest. Flávio is described as a candidate seeking a running mate, reflecting his search for allies in the 2026 election race. The tone is satirical and focused on the emotional dynamics between the two political figures.

item.title: Podcast discute o que Flávio Bolsonaro pode querer com mentira sobre as urnas
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) raised unfounded suspicions about electronic voting machines during an event with foreign diplomats, repeating the fraud narrative previously used by his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, in 2022. The incident occurred four years after the former president’s attack on the voting system during a meeting with ambassadors. The podcast examines the motivations behind electoral disinformation by members of the Bolsonaro family.

item.title: Aliados criticam estratégia de Flávio Bolsonaro após fala sobre urnas
item.description: Allies criticize Flávio Bolsonaro's strategy after he claimed Brazilian electronic voting machines originate from the Venezuelan company Smartmatic, a claim already debunked by the TSE. Despite saying he does not question the voting system, his remarks caused a rift in the pre-campaign, hindering dialogue with moderate voters and alliance-building. Party leaders view the episode as a strategic misstep, attempting to distance themselves from the case that led to Jair Bolsonaro's ineligibility.

item.title: Dividido entre Lula e Flávio, Centrão caminha para ficar neutro no 1º turno
item.description: The so-called 'Centrão' is moving toward formal neutrality in Brazil's 2026 presidential election, choosing to focus resources on congressional races rather than backing either Lula or Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round. Despite being courted by both campaigns, Centrist parties are avoiding explicit endorsements to protect local candidacies, adopting a pragmatic stance that shifts by region. While the PT is leaning left for its national ticket, the PL made aggressive efforts — including offering the vice-presidency — to win Centrão support, but was rebuffed, notably by the PP.

item.title: O coração de Flávio Bolsonaro bate mais rápido. O de Lula, menos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro once led Lula in polling simulations for both first and second rounds, but the latest Quaest poll shows Lula winning 45% to 37% in a second-round scenario, reversing earlier trends, particularly in the Southeast where Flávio had a 12-point lead in April. The text emphasizes that parliamentary amendments (60 billion reais) are used to buy political support and sustain electoral patronage, without ensuring democratic legitimacy.

item.title: Jorge Oliveira seria o 1º indicado de Flávio ao STF, apostam aliados
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro state that TCU Minister Jorge Oliveira would be the first nominee to the STF if the senator wins the 2026 presidential election. They emphasize Oliveira’s decades-long relationship of trust with the Bolsonaro family, including his roles as legal advisor and chief of staff to Eduardo Bolsonaro and as Minister of the General Secretariat of the Presidency under Jair Bolsonaro. Oliveira’s appointment to the STF would allow Flávio to nominate a new TCU minister, with allies pointing to Wagner Rosario as a potential successor.

item.title: Centrão deixa Flávio à deriva para preservar capital político em 2027
item.description: The PP and União Brasil have chosen to remain neutral in the first round of the 2026 presidential election to preserve their political capital and maintain leverage with any future government, aiming to influence the legislative agenda and the 2027 elections for the presidency of the Chamber and Senate. This decision leaves Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) without the support of the center-right federation he sought, following the rejection of his vice-presidential offer to Senator Tereza Cristina and deteriorating relations with PP leadership, especially after the PF operation targeting the party’s president. Neutrality applies only to the first round, with potential revision in the second depending on election results.

item.title: Partidos e presidente, nada a ver
item.description: The 2026 presidential election may not secure legislative support for the winner, as party structures prioritize their own interests over national ones. Although Congress is expected to remain right-leaning, neither a right-wing president like Flávio Bolsonaro nor a hypothetical left-wing Lula victory would guarantee legislative backing. This disconnect between presidential vote and legislative composition reveals a crisis of representation and partisan alignment.

item.title: STM deve julgar expulsão de Bolsonaro das Forças Armadas só depois das eleições
item.description: The Superior Military Tribunal (STM) is expected to postpone the judgment on the possible expulsion of Jair Bolsonaro, Walter Braga Netto, Paulo Sérgio Nogueira, Augusto Heleno, and Almir Garnier Santos from the Armed Forces until after the 2026 presidential elections. All were convicted by the STF in the coup plot case and now face the risk of losing their military rank and status in military justice. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Moraes manda PF prender técnica agrícola por descumprir cautelares
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered the arrest of agricultural technician Taís Simone Prado Leal for violating precautionary measures in the January 8 case. She had previously signed a non-prosecution agreement with the PGR, but it was revoked after the PF found evidence of broader involvement, including messages suggesting the use of CACs (collectors, sport shooters, and hunters) to remove Lula from power and geolocation data placing her at the Ministries Esplanade on January 8. The arrest followed her failure to comply with electronic monitoring, despite multiple attempts by Pernambuco’s prison secretariat to locate her.

item.title: O alerta vermelho dos evangélicos para Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Evangelical leaders close to Flávio Bolsonaro are pessimistic about how evangelical voters are responding to his candidacy, signaling a potential challenge in securing support from this key demographic. The article raises a red alert about the senator’s ability to retain the religious base that propelled his family’s political rise.

item.title: Valdemar rejeita chapa pura para Flávio após União-PP adotar neutralidade
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL, stated that the party cannot launch a pure ticket for Flávio Bolsonaro after the União-PP federation adopted neutrality in the 2026 presidential election. He reiterated his preference for Senator Tereza Cristina as running mate, despite her refusal, and acknowledged the difficulty in attracting allies, with only the Republicans still open. Valdemar also cited Michelle Bolsonaro's resistance as an obstacle to the pre-campaign, though he believes she will ultimately run for Senate.

item.title: Cúpula do Republicanos fala em ‘portas se fechando’ para negociação com Flávio após desgastes
item.description: The leadership of the Republicans party stated that negotiations for an alliance with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) in the 2026 presidential race are closing due to campaign wear and tear and difficulties in forming state-level alliances. A decision may be made by August 5, the deadline for party conventions. Cited factors include controversies involving the senator, such as alleged ties to Daniel Vorcaro, failure to disclose finances for the film 'Dark Horse', public disagreement with Michelle Bolsonaro, actions during Trump’s tariff imposition, and doubts about electronic voting security.

item.title: Lula deve evitar estados com palanques divididos em agendas no primeiro turno
item.description: President Lula should avoid visiting states with multiple electoral slates during the first round of the 2026 elections to prevent discomfort among allies, as agreed with his campaign team. The decision may be revised due to pressure from local candidates and evolving electoral dynamics. States like Pernambuco, Maranhão and Paraíba exemplify divided support, creating internal tensions.

item.title: O 'tio do churrasco' é uma mulher
item.description: Brazilian voters aged 60 or older are predominantly female (55%), diverse in occupation and political affiliation, and defy the stereotype of the 'barbecue uncle' as a monolithic, right-leaning bloc. Though television remains their main information source, their voting behavior is driven by protecting pensions, health, and household stability — not ideology — with recent polls showing strong support for Lula despite a notable conservative segment. Their vote functions as a form of insurance, not speculation, aimed at safeguarding what they’ve built, not reacting to fear or nostalgia.

item.title: Pressionado, Flávio Bolsonaro enfrenta desembarque de União-PP enquanto testa discurso mais radical
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) is facing mounting pressure after losing the support of the PP and, by extension, União Brasil, due to campaign wear and declining poll numbers. In response, he has adopted a more radical rhetoric, emulating his father and spreading false claims about electronic voting machines, which is alienating more moderate allies.

item.title: Após ataques a Flávio, Caiado intensifica estratégia de se opor ao bolsonarismo mirando também Eduardo
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado intensified his strategy of opposing Bolsonarism by publicly attacking both Flávio and Eduardo Bolsonaro. He labeled Eduardo the 'Pateta of Brazilian politics' following U.S. tariff announcements, accusing them of focusing on electronic voting machine controversies instead of Brazil's economic interests, particularly agribusiness. Caiado framed his stance as a defense of national industry, exports, and jobs, even launching a poll on X to reinforce the narrative.

item.title: Para ministros do STF e TSE, crítica de Flávio às urnas foi proposital
item.description: Ministers from the STF, STJ, and TSE assess that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s criticism of electronic voting machines was intentional, part of a strategy to signal alignment with the Trump administration and major tech firms to gain international support during the 2026 presidential campaign. His remarks, made at an event with ambassadors, repeated unfounded claims about the Venezuelan origin of Brazil’s voting machines and were described as a 'premeditated case,' not spontaneous.

item.title: União Brasil oficializa ACM Neto como candidato ao governo da Bahia
item.description: União Brasil officially nominated ACM Neto as its candidate for governor of Bahia during a party convention in Salvador, with Zé Cocá (PP) as his running mate for vice-governor. The ticket also named Ângelo Coronel (Republicanos) and João Roma (PL) for the Senate. ACM Neto, former mayor of Salvador and grandson of ex-governor Antônio Carlos Magalhães, reached the runoff in 2022 and is now returning to the race with a message of change and hope.

item.title: Flávio usa método Trump sobre urnas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is repeating Donald Trump's false claims about electronic voting machines to lay the groundwork for contesting a potential defeat in the 2026 elections. He did so in a meeting with ambassadors, despite being entangled in controversies including alleged payments to Daniel Vorcaro, canceled invoices tied to the Master network, difficulties forming alliances, and family conflict with his stepmother Michelle Bolsonaro.

item.title: Governo Lula insiste em negociação de tarifaço, mas só vê chances de avanço após eleições no Brasil e no Congresso dos EUA
item.description: The Lula government hopes to resume trade talks with the U.S. after July 29 but expects only meaningful progress after Brazil’s presidential elections and the U.S. midterms in November, citing current political vulnerability. Lula stated that despite attempting to negotiate in good faith, there was no reciprocity from the U.S., which prioritized electoral agenda over economic dialogue, demanding unilateral market openings in key sectors without concessions. Brazil, however, remains committed to the negotiation table, anticipating that a shift in Congressional power balance could improve conditions for dialogue.

item.title: Priscila Costa deixa disputa a vaga ao Senado em 2026
item.description: Federal Deputy Priscila Costa (PL-CE) withdrew from the 2026 Senate race after losing influence within her party amid a crisis between Michelle Bolsonaro and the faction led by André Fernandes, which backed Alcides Fernandes for the Senate. According to her office, the decision was imposed by the PL, not self-initiated, and she will instead run for re-election to the Chamber of Deputies. Priscila is expected to comment on the matter in the coming days.

item.title: Governo Lula afrouxa restrições por lei eleitoral, e EBC republica parte de conteúdo tirado do ar
item.description: The Lula government has eased communication restrictions imposed in early July on ministers and federal agencies to avoid electoral violations, following complaints that the rules were hindering administrative work. The move comes during the 'electoral defrost' period, when restrictions on government publicity are tightened to prevent undue advantages in the 2026 election campaign.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro repete tese falsa sobre urnas desde 2014 alternando ataques e recuos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro has repeated since 2014 the false claim that Brazilian electronic voting machines originate from the Venezuelan company Smartmatic, a narrative he first used as a state deputy in Rio de Janeiro. On Tuesday (21), he presented this misinformation to ambassadors, reviving a discourse that alternates attacks on the electoral system with occasional retractions. The claim is widely regarded as false by electoral authorities and security experts.

item.title: Alckmin sobre tarifaço dos EUA: "Objetivo é resolver o problema"
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin stated that Brazil's goal is not to retaliate against the 25% U.S. tariffs but to seek a negotiated solution, emphasizing there is no intention of a trade war. He noted that negotiations with the USTR are ongoing and criticized, without naming, 'bad Brazilians' spreading misleading information that harms the economy — an apparent reference to Flávio Bolsonaro. President Lula has signed a provisional measure allocating R$18.5 billion to support affected sectors.

item.title: "Temos que sair dessa discussão", diz Tarcísio sobre urnas eletrônicas
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas defended the reliability of Brazil's electronic voting machines after Flávio Bolsonaro raised unsubstantiated claims linking them to the Venezuelan company Smartmatic, previously debunked by the TSE. He urged moving past the unproductive debate to focus on national projects. Tarcísio also stated that Flávio has no connection to the U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods.

item.title: Tarcísio diz confiar nas urnas após fala de Flávio Bolsonaro em evento com embaixadores
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas expressed confidence in Brazil's electronic voting machines in response to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's unsubstantiated claims linking Brazilian urns to alleged manipulation in Venezuela. Tarcísio stated his trust in the electoral system is fundamental to his candidacy and urged focus on policy debates rather than baseless theories. Flávio Bolsonaro's remarks prompted a legal challenge from the Brazil of Hope Federation (PT, PCdoB, PV) before the TSE, accusing him of spreading known falsehoods about the electoral system.

item.title: Em SP, Tarcísio diz que confia nas urnas e Flávio precisa abandonar 'discussão que não leva a lugar nenhum'
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas said he trusts electronic voting machines and urged Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to stop the unfounded fraud debate, calling it unproductive. He also addressed the U.S. 25% tariff on Brazilian exports, advocating for negotiations with the U.S. government and rejecting economic reciprocity laws, stating Brazil must defend its interests through dialogue, not retaliation.

item.title: Volta a circular fala de Caiado dizendo não precisar de bolsonaristas
item.description: A video from March 2020 resurfaced showing Goiás Governor Ronaldo Caiado confronting Bolsonarist protesters during the pandemic, stating he did not need their votes and prioritizing public health measures as a doctor. He was heckled by demonstrators but defended his stance on restricting gatherings to curb coronavirus spread, even opposing President Bolsonaro’s stance. The clip has resurfaced amid 2026 pre-campaign tensions, with Caiado as a PSD presidential pre-candidate and having criticized Flávio Bolsonaro’s recent diplomatic engagement.

item.title: Por que Lula recalculou a rota sobre tarifaço dos Estados Unidos
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva recalibrated his strategy in response to the 25% U.S. tariff after strong backlash from the productive sector, which criticized the political use of the trade dispute. The government abandoned confrontational rhetoric and shifted focus to negotiating with Washington, offering R$18.5 billion in credit lines for exporters and seeking alternative markets to mitigate tariff impacts.

item.title: Flávio golpista: o moderado é cabeça de bacalhau da “zelite” sem miolo
item.description: The article criticizes Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) for maintaining a coupist discourse and threatening the STF, repeating his father's lies about the Brazilian electoral system before foreign diplomats. He is portrayed as a 'centrist extremist' attempting to appear moderate but failing to convince, unlike Tarcísio de Freitas, seen as the true candidate of 'moderate Bolsonarismo'. The author suggests the Bolsonaro family would rather lose to Lula than support an outsider as successor, and that Flávio lost backing after financial scandal revelations.

item.title: Zema defende voto impresso como complemento à urna eletrônica
item.description: Romeu Zema advocated for the implementation of a printed receipt in electronic voting machines as a complement to enhance electoral reliability, proposing that a sample of machines produce a sealed physical record for later verification. He affirmed having been elected and re-elected via electronic voting and considers the current system reliable, but supports improvements. His remarks came in response to unfounded claims by Flávio Bolsonaro, who falsely alleged CIA documentation of vote manipulation in Venezuela’s 2010 elections and linked it to Brazilian voting machines, a claim debunked by the TSE in 2020.

item.title: O que Ronaldo Caiado tentou mostrar ao criticar Flávio e Eduardo Bolsonaro
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado criticized Flávio Bolsonaro for reviving the claim of electronic ballot fraud, arguing it wasted a chance to discuss economic development with foreign ambassadors. He also indirectly questioned Eduardo Bolsonaro’s green card, implying Brazilian politicians should prioritize national interests over personal ones, and used a Disney metaphor to mock him. Caiado aims to position himself as a moderate alternative to radical Bolsonarism, focusing on economic and institutional agendas.

item.title: UP lança Vivian Mendes ao governo de SP com chapa puro-sangue em convenção estadual em SP
item.description: The Popular Unity (UP) party held its state convention in São Paulo and officially nominated Vivian Mendes as its candidate for governor of São Paulo in 2026, with Marcelo Pereira as her running mate. The party also confirmed candidates for the Senate (Maira de Souza and Marcio Alves), Chamber of Deputies (including Ricardo Senese), and the State Legislative Assembly. Mendes, who previously ran for Senate in 2022 and was detained during a protest against the privatization of Sabesp in 2023, leads the party's 'pure-blood' ticket.

item.title: Mudança na TV: BandNews completa 25 anos com novidades na grade e cenário tecnológico
item.description: BandNews TV celebrated its 25th anniversary with a complete programming overhaul and the launch of a state-of-the-art studio at Grupo Bandeirantes' headquarters in Morumbi. The new schedule strengthens political, economic, and business coverage, featuring commentators like Luiz Felipe Pondé and Reinaldo Azevedo, and reshuffled newscasts aimed at deepening factual analysis ahead of the elections. The launch event was attended by Vice President Geraldo Alckmin, Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, and Mayor Ricardo Nunes.

item.title: TSE recomenda que tribunais eleitorais firmem parcerias com especialistas em IA
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) recommended that regional electoral courts establish technical cooperation agreements with institutions specializing in artificial intelligence, digital forensics, and content analysis. The measure aims to strengthen the technical capacity of the Electoral Justice in producing evidence in cases involving disinformation and synthetic content. The goal is to ensure greater effectiveness in combating information manipulation during the electoral process.

item.title: Tarifaço: Alckmin diz que Lei de Reprocidade 'está na mesa', mas que objetivo não é 'fazer guerra comercial, e sim resolver problema'
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin stated that while the Reciprocity Law is available as an instrument, the government's goal is not retaliation or a trade war, but to resolve the issue of U.S. tariffs on Brazilian products through negotiation. He emphasized Brazil’s pursuit of dialogue and new markets to avoid escalation. President Lula reinforced that Brazil remains at the negotiating table despite the lack of U.S. reciprocity and will not abandon diplomatic efforts to address the matter.

item.title: União Brasil lança candidatura de ACM Neto ao governo da Bahia
item.description: ACM Neto was launched as the União Brasil candidate for governor of Bahia, with Zé Cocá as his running mate and alliances with Republicanos, PL, Novo, Podemos, PMN and the Progressista, PSDB-Cidadania and Renovação Solidária federations. He reinforced support for Ronaldo Caiado in the first round of the presidential race, with potential backing for Flávio Bolsonaro in a possible runoff against Lula. ACM Neto accused the Jerônimo Rodrigues administration of losing control of public safety and sought to avoid nationalizing the debate, citing a technical tie with the incumbent governor in recent polls.

item.title: Cúpula do PL vê erro de Flávio ao repetir discurso de Bolsonaro sobre urnas e o orienta a abandonar o tema
item.description: The PL leadership advised Flávio Bolsonaro to stop discussing electronic voting machines, arguing that repeating his father Jair Bolsonaro’s 2022 strategy causes more political harm than benefit and undermines his attempt to project moderation. Party officials believe the topic fails to expand the electorate beyond the Bolsonarist base and recommend focusing on economy, security, inflation, jobs, and cost of living to appeal to undecided voters.

item.title: Caiado e Renan Santos criticam Flávio Bolsonaro por falas em reunião com embaixadores
item.description: Pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) and candidate Renan Santos (Missão) criticized Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) for his remarks on electronic voting machines made during a meeting with ambassadors, defending the integrity of Brazil's electoral system.

item.title: “Flávio é o único que tem condições de derrotar o Lula”, diz Moro
item.description: Senator Sergio Moro (PL) stated that Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) is the only right-wing figure capable of defeating President Lula (PT) in the 2026 elections. Moro emphasized that defeating Lula is a national necessity for the country. The comment was made on January 22nd in support of Flávio Bolsonaro’s pré-candidacy for governor of Paraná.
